Business goal: Return durable settings truth for one curated page so the operator workspace can inspect and edit page configuration honestly.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can load page settings for the selected page and see effective icon, top-nav visibility, template intent, and curated context-nav targets.
Notes / constraints: The settings record attaches only to an existing curated page. It does not own page placement, module landing-page selection, or discovery truth. If no explicit context-nav rows exist, the effective fallback is a self-only context-nav item.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may read page settings.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may reveal the Page Settings panel. Hidden UI does not replace backend enforcement.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before page-settings reads. The feature must validate the selected page id, load the one-to-one settings record if present, project effective fallback values, and reject missing or inaccessible pages honestly.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-admin browser-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may disable the panel when permission is missing, but backend enforcement remains authoritative.
Request contract: Exact page id only. Clients may not query arbitrary mutable labels as identity.
Response contract: Returns selected-page settings, effective fallback values, approved current context-nav membership, and enough metadata to render the Page Settings section without changing topology truth.
Error contract: 400 invalid page id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 page not found or not eligible for settings.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes a narrow page-reader seam from `webAppHierarchyBuilder` to validate that the target page exists and remains eligible for settings.
Persistence impact: Adds durable page-settings and context-nav membership reads. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique one-to-one settings row per `webAppPageId`. Unique context-nav membership per owner/target pair. Exact-read index on `webAppPageId`.
Search / filter model: Exact read only in v1. No broad fuzzy search required.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive read seam. Must not silently reinterpret existing topology-owned `templateKey` rules while migration posture remains transitional.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local exact-read validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected same-origin root-admin shell.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is optional for exact settings reads.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores and returns internal page-configuration metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are high because the capability exposes durable navigation/config truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can load truthful page settings for a selected curated page without confusing settings truth with topology truth.

Business goal: Persist durable page settings so governed navigation and template choices are not trapped in frontend-only state.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can save icon selection, top-nav visibility, page-template intent, and curated context-nav membership for a selected page.
Notes / constraints: The capability must enforce the approved icon and template catalogs, preserve the default self-only context-nav fallback when no explicit targets are supplied, and reject system-managed fields. It must not update page placement or canonical page label.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may update page settings.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose save actions. Disabled UI is not sufficient enforcement.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before settings mutation. The feature must validate allowed fields, normalize and replace context-nav membership deterministically, preserve `updatedAt`, and reject invalid catalog keys or missing target pages.
Frontend states: draft edit; validation error; save success; save failure; denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-admin browser-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may prevent invalid submission locally, but backend remains the final validator.
Request contract: Body allows only `iconKey`, `showInTopNav`, `topNavOrder`, `pageTemplateKey`, and explicit context-nav target page ids with order. Clients may not submit ids or timestamps.
Response contract: Returns the updated settings record, effective context-nav projection, and selected-page summary needed by the workspace.
Error contract: 400 invalid catalog key, invalid context-nav target, duplicate target, or malformed payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 page not found; 409 transition conflict or unsupported migration posture.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes `webAppHierarchyBuilder` public seams to validate target pages and page eligibility; may reuse approved hierarchy/planner reads rather than scanning frontend implementation.
Persistence impact: Creates or updates one durable settings row and replaces or preserves explicit context-nav membership rows.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique one-to-one settings row per page. Unique context-nav target membership per owner page. Deterministic ordering index on owner page plus `sortOrder`.
Compatibility / migration notes: Compatibility is required by default. The slice must coexist with the current topology-owned `templateKey` posture and should not silently break existing materialization flows while migration remains incomplete.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local mutation validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected root-admin shell.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is recommended because this is a privileged configuration mutation.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; stores internal navigation/template configuration metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and configuration-integrity relevance are high because this changes durable operator-controlled navigation behavior.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can save governed page settings through exact validated inputs and the saved state remains durable and deterministic.

Business goal: Expose approved option catalogs so the operator workspace does not hardcode icon and template choices or invent invalid context-nav targets.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can load the approved icon catalog, approved page-template catalog, and selectable page targets for the selected page-settings workflow.
Notes / constraints: The icon catalog should come from the signed-off design-system icon-catalog or icon-picker source when that pattern is ready. The selectable page target list should be projected from `webAppHierarchyBuilder` curated tree truth rather than from a separate page-catalog feature. The capability must not infer discovered app truth or allow arbitrary custom icon payloads.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may read page-settings option catalogs.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose page-settings options.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before options reads. The feature must return approved icon keys from the governed design-system catalog source when available, approved template keys, default fallback metadata, and eligible context-nav target pages projected from curated hierarchy/tree seams.
Frontend states: loading options; loaded options; error; denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-admin browser-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may cache options, but backend remains the source of truth for approved choices.
Request contract: Exact selected page id in query or route scope only. No freeform search in v1.
Response contract: Returns approved icon catalog, default icon metadata, approved template catalog, and eligible context-nav target page summaries for the selected page.
Error contract: 400 invalid page id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 selected page not found.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes a narrow `webAppHierarchyBuilder` page-reader or planner-style seam derived from curated tree truth for eligible target pages; does not depend on `webAppSurfaceDiscovery` for options truth.
Indexes / uniqueness: Exact-read index support for selected page validation only. Icon-catalog source may begin as a checked-in governed manifest until the signed-off design-system pattern is ready. Selectable page targets come from curated tree truth rather than a separate durable page catalog.
Search / filter model: Exact and scoped options read only in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive read seam. Must preserve future ability to switch from a simple selector to a governed icon-grid UI without changing durable settings semantics.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local options validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected root-admin shell.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is optional.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; returns internal catalog and curated-page metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are moderate to high because the options catalog defines what the UI may legally submit.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when the operator workspace can load approved icon/template choices and eligible context-nav targets without hardcoded frontend truth.

Business goal: Let operators choose which direct child page should be the landing page for a module without pretending that choice is page-settings truth.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can set or clear one module landing page and know that module entry will resolve to that direct child page.
Notes / constraints: This capability is topology-owned, not settings-owned. The landing page must be a direct child page of the module. Modules remain structural containers in v1.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may update module landing-page selection.
Frontend visibility rule: Only authorized operator surfaces may expose module landing-page actions in the Hierarchy section.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before module landing-page mutation. The feature must validate the module, validate that the target page is a direct child of that module, update the module seam, and reject descendant or cross-module targets.
Frontend states: loading; edit; save success; validation error; denied
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-admin browser-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: UI may guide the user toward valid direct-child targets, but backend validation remains authoritative.
Request contract: Body allows nullable `landingPageWebAppPageId` only. Clients may not submit module-owned system fields.
Response contract: Returns updated module summary including landing-page selection state.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 module or target page not found; 409 target page not a direct child of the module.
Cross-feature seams: May reuse existing page and module readers inside the hierarchy feature. Does not depend on the settings feature for authority.
Persistence impact: Adds nullable module landing-page truth to curated topology.
Indexes / uniqueness: Nullable exact landing-page foreign key on module row or approved child seam. Integrity check that target page belongs to the same module and has `module-root` placement.
Compatibility / migration notes: Additive topology seam. Must not silently reinterpret module routes or module structural ownership semantics.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and hierarchy-local topology validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct new CSP posture beyond the existing protected root-admin shell.
Audit requirement: Audit denied attempts through shared authz visibility. Success-side audit is recommended because this changes durable navigation entry behavior.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal topology metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are high because this changes durable module-entry behavior.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can set or clear one direct-child landing page for a module and invalid targets are rejected honestly.

Business goal: Expose the first real operator workflow for editing page settings inside the governed hierarchy workspace without bloating the route into a custom admin fork.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can select a page in `/root-admin#web-app-hierarchy`, open the `Page Settings` section, review approved choices, save settings, and see truthful success, error, and denied states.
Notes / constraints: The route stays one workspace. The operator-facing sections are `Hierarchy`, `Page Settings`, `Observed App`, and `Preview & Apply`. This slice only adds the selected-page Page Settings section and adjacent module landing-page affordance; it does not redefine discovery or materialization ownership. Real-app UI must use approved design-system families only.
Tenant context rule: Root-operated browser workspace outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies.
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capabilities
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may use the page-settings workspace flow.
Frontend visibility rule: The page-settings panel and module landing-page controls should be hidden or disabled when capabilities are missing, while denied states remain truthful if direct requests occur.
Backend enforcement rule: Root-admin browser session bootstrap and protected API calls remain authoritative. The shell must not invent successful local state when backend save fails or permission is denied.
Frontend surface: governed hierarchy workspace with selected-page Page Settings panel
Frontend states: selected page; loading settings; loading options; dirty form; save success; save failure; denied; selected module landing-page edit; empty/unselected state
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing root-admin browser-session expiry and same-origin protected-shell posture.
Client-side permission behavior: Client-side visibility and dirty-state behavior improve UX only; all authority remains server-side.
Request contract: Requests exact selected-page or selected-module scope only and submits governed form fields only.
Response contract: Renders saved settings and module-landing state from backend responses rather than optimistic invented truth.
Error contract: Uses existing root-admin error handling plus feature-owned validation/denied messages from backend APIs.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes governed hierarchy-tree behavior, existing root-admin shell chrome, and approved form/drawer patterns. If icon-grid design is not signed off, use an already approved selector pattern in v1.
Persistence impact: No direct browser persistence beyond current shell state. Server-side settings and module-landing truth become the durable source.
Indexes / uniqueness: No new frontend search index required. Browser state remains scoped to the selected page or module. Any selector ordering should match backend-provided order.
Search / filter model: No fuzzy browser search required in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Must preserve backward-compatible shell posture and must not bypass the design-system signoff rule for new UI patterns.
Authorization enforcement layer: Protected root-admin shell plus backend authz on every save/read route.
CSP / browser security impact: Must remain inside the current same-origin CSP and shell security posture. No new third-party asset requirements should be introduced for icon choice in v1.
Audit requirement: Denied route/API attempts should remain audit-visible through backend enforcement. Frontend-only display changes do not replace audit.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; shows operator-facing internal app-configuration metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and governed-frontend anti-drift relevance are high because this is a privileged real operator workflow.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can manage page settings inside the governed hierarchy workspace without introducing a route-local fork of the shell or bypassing backend authority.
